findings.title: Where the brief entries get `category` and the folded trigger is not pinned
findings.detail: SPEC-0201 defines the brief's `must_fix` entries as the combiner's must-fix findings with `persona` added, and SPEC-0203 replaces the combiner. This spec only says the brief is "built where SPEC-0201/0203 build the brief". `render_pending_brief` reads `item['detail']`, so the combiner has to call `finding_detail(f)` and carry `category` when it builds the entries. Name the function that does this (`combine_reviews` today, its SPEC-0203 replacement later) and say the AC5 brief test goes through it, not through a hand-built brief.

findings.title: Single-reviewer brief path is not covered
findings.detail: SPEC-0201 says that with exactly one reviewer the brief is SPEC-0187's: `source` is the persona, `must_fix` entries have no `persona`, and the `fix_brief` has no `[persona]` prefix. A user who opts in with `reviewers: [adversarial_reviewer]`, which AC3 explicitly allows for `frugal`, gets that path. Say whether `category` and the folded trigger must also reach that brief, and keep AC6's "labelled `[adversarial_reviewer]`" scoped to two or more reviewers.

findings.title: Trigger rule is prompt-only and `finding_detail` hides a missing trigger
findings.detail: The spec accepts that "a finding without a trigger is at most `minor`" is only a prompt rule, and AC1's test only checks that the template contains the rule. A cheap code check would help: for example, record the severity downgrade, or log a `finding` note when a `must_fix` has no `trigger`. Otherwise a trigger-less false-positive `must_fix` forces an implementer loop (up to `loop_max`) with nothing marking it as unverified. This is optional, because the spec records the choice as accepted.

findings.title: Say that a failed `try` leaves `changed_files` as `None`, rendered as `(none)`
findings.detail: "A failure there leaves all three unset" and AC4's "`(none)` on `GitError`" agree only because `_as_text(None)` returns `(none)` (personas.py:156). One sentence would make that explicit. The ordering and cap rules (sort, keep 300, `… N more`) are clear.

findings.title: `status: accepted` while still under review
findings.detail: The spec is already `accepted` at the point where it is being reviewed for admission, and the "Open questions" section says none remain. This is fine if intentional; the lifecycle in the schema doc says review comes before acceptance.
